To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inelasticity of pion-nucleon scattering in vacuum and in nuclear matter is crucial to obtain a consistent picture of the vector meson mass shift and that the in-medium properties of the vector mesons are determined by the density dependence of the ρ- N and ω- N amplitudes.

1) the pion is strongly absorbed in nuclear matter at low energies; 2) the ρ and the ω mesons are strongly absorbed in nuclear medium at low energies and their spectral function is considerably broadened; 3) the ρ-ω mixing is strongly enhanced in nuclear matter.

1) the ρ- N interaction in nuclear matter is attractive at small nuclear density; 2) the ρ-mass is shifted to lower energy; 3) the ω- N interaction is repulsive at small nuclear density and the ω-mass is shifted upwards in energy. [1]
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the in-medium modifications of hadrons, in particular of vector mesons, and their role as mediators for the nuclear force.
a unified description of the pion-nucleon scattering amplitude in vacuum and in nuclear matter, including the in-medium modifications of the ρ-omega and kaon-nucleon scattering.
the following topics: 1) The pion-nucleon scattering amplitude in a relativistic coupled-channel approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vector meson mass shifts in nuclear matter are not large, and are not attractive.
the vector mesons in medium are not simply shifted in mass but are strongly affected by the medium.
the ρ mass is reduced in nuclear matter by 50-60 MeV at normal density and by 70-80 MeV at 3ρ _{o}.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vector mesons are not simply dressed nucleons but rather have a more complicated structure.
our approach provides a unified description for pion nucleon and vector meson scattering and nuclear physics.
the ρ and the ω are not ‘free’ in the medium, but they are strongly coupled to the nucleon-hole continuum. [1]
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ρ and the ω mass shifts in nuclear matter are not universal.
the in-medium properties of the ω and ρ meson are very sensitive to the in-medium properties (and hence to the dynamics) of the nucleon resonances.
the ρ and the ω mass shift are very sensitive to the details of the pion and vector meson interaction in vacuum and to the in-medium modification of the pion-nucleon amplitude.
